# Cammakkhandhaka (Kd 5)

**ID:** Kd 5
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Cammakkhandhaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m2.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cammakkhandhaka* ("The chapter on skins" or "On hides") is the fifth section of the Khandhaka division of the Vinaya Piṭaka [Norman 1983]. The text regulates the monastic use of footwear, leather, animal skins, vehicles, and beds, and defines the geographic boundaries of the "middle country" (*majjhimadesa*) while setting out relaxed Vinaya rules for monks living in border regions [Banerjee 1979]. Centered in its narrative frame are the accounts of two prominent monks: Soṇa Koḷivisa, renowned as the Buddha's foremost disciple in exerting energy, and Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa, who received ordination in the remote region of Avantī [Banerjee 1979]. The text is accompanied by traditional commentary, including the Chinese *Samantapāsādikā* (*Shan-Chien-P'i-P'o-Sha*), which preserves exegesis on the meritorious background of Soṇa [Bapat & Hirakawa 1970].

 DharmaNexus also detects extensive internal Vinaya reuse with Khandhaka chapters such as the *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15), *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* (Kd 6), and *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), as well as cross-language matches in the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, the Sanskrit *Carmavastu*, and the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* [DharmaNexus].
